question: What did Boethius, awaiting execution, say separates the eternal from the merely endless?
answer: Having it all at once. Eternity, he wrote in The Consolation of Philosophy around 524, is the whole of an endless life possessed together and complete. A world with no beginning or end would still live one moment at a time, losing yesterday and not yet holding tomorrow: everlasting, not eternal.
move: More of the same is not a different kind of thing.
source: Boethius, The Consolation of Philosophy, V.6
reference: Boethius, The Consolation of Philosophy V.6, trans. Walsh, Oxford University Press, 1999
